title: The Renaissance masters
examples: Who was the most famous artist of the Renaissance?
What is the difference between realism and humanism in art?
Can you compare the styles of Leonardo and Michelangelo?

explain.say: Today we learn about great Renaissance masters. These artists changed art forever. We will look at Leonardo da Vinci first.
Next we study Michelangelo. He was famous for his powerful sculptures. Think about the statue of David. He showed amazing human form.
Raphael was also a master painter. His work often showed beautiful and calm scenes. He painted many figures together. Think of his Madonnas.
Realism in art means painting things as they look. Artists tried to copy the real world accurately. They paid close attention to details. This made the art look very real.
Humanism was a focus on human potential. It celebrated human achievements and life. Artists started focusing on people and human stories. This was a big shift in thinking.
In everyday life, think about portrait photography. A good portrait tries to capture the person's true likeness. This uses realism, just like the masters did.

faq.q: What is the main difference between Renaissance art and earlier art styles?
faq.a: Earlier art was often more symbolic and religious. Renaissance art focused more on realistic human figures and life.
asks: How did art change during the Renaissance?
Did Renaissance art look more like real life?

faq.q: Who was responsible for the Mona Lisa?
faq.a: Leonardo da Vinci painted the famous portrait known as the Mona Lisa. It is a masterpiece of portraiture.
asks: Which master painted the Mona Lisa?
Who painted that famous woman portrait?

faq.q: What does humanism mean for art?
faq.a: Humanism meant that art started celebrating human life and capability. People became the focus, not just religious stories.
asks: Was humanism about people in art?
What did humanism bring to art subjects?

faq.q: Did all the masters paint in the same style?
faq.a: No, each master had a unique style. Leonardo was known for softness, Michelangelo for strength, and Raphael for harmony.
asks: Were the masters all the same?
How were the masters different from each other?

faq.q: Was realism only about looking real?
faq.a: It was about more than just looking real. It meant understanding human anatomy and emotion accurately.

facts: The Renaissance period saw a rebirth of classical learning.
Leonardo da Vinci was a polymath, meaning he excelled in many fields.
Humanism placed value on human reason and potential.
Michelangelo's work often emphasized the idealized human body.

quiz.say: Which master is most associated with the painting of the Mona Lisa?
quiz.why: Leonardo da Vinci is the artist who created the famous Mona Lisa portrait.

wrong.0: This option is too vague; the full name is needed for accuracy.
wrong.2: Michelangelo focused more on large sculptures, not this specific portrait.
wrong.3: Raphael is famous for group scenes, not this specific solo portrait.

quiz.say: Art that focuses on human potential and achievement is called:
quiz.why: Humanism shifted focus from purely divine matters to human experience.

wrong.1: Realism describes the style of depiction, not the underlying philosophy.
wrong.2: Classicism refers to the influence of ancient Greece and Rome.
wrong.3: Polymathy describes a person who knows many things, not the art movement itself.

quiz.say: If an artist accurately depicts the proportions of the human body, they are using:
quiz.why: Realism requires careful observation to make the subject look true to life.

wrong.1: Humanism is the idea behind the art, not the technique of depiction.
wrong.2: Symmetry is a quality of the art, but realism is the overall goal of accuracy.
wrong.3: Perspective is a tool used to create depth, but realism is the overall goal.
